players.product: infrared and visible optical components, Black Diamond infrared glass (used instead of germanium), assemblies and modules, and infrared cameras

quarterly_data.signal: LightPath's fiscal Q4 2026 results release (8-K exhibit) details the July follow-on orders: an $11 million follow-on infrared camera order from a leading global technology customer for counter-unmanned aircraft system (UAS) applications and $13 million in follow-on optical assembly orders from a leading counter-UAS and defense systems supplier (neither named). Q4 infrared components growth included $1.1 million of infrared materials sales from AML (acquired January 2026); engineering services rose on higher recognition against Visimid Technologies' Lockheed Martin contract. CEO Sam Rubin: with AML LightPath now operates two domestic glass production sites and roughly 20 proprietary infrared compositions. He cites legislation enacted in December 2025 directing the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a strategy to eliminate the Department of Defense's reliance on any covered nation for optical glass or optical systems, with a January 1, 2030 deadline for implementing the strategy; because supplier qualification cycles run two to three years, sourcing decisions are being considered and made now.
quarterly_data.figure: $11 million follow-on infrared camera order; $13 million follow-on optical assembly orders; AML infrared materials sales $1.1 million in Q4; roughly 20 proprietary infrared compositions
